title: The imperfetto
description: Formation of the imperfect tense and its uses: habits, descriptions and background.
objectives: Form the imperfetto of regular verbs and of essere, fare, dire, bere.
Use it for habits in the past and for descriptions.
Recognise it in stories: C'era una volta…
Recognise the polite, intentional, counterfactual (colloquial) and reported uses of the imperfetto.

blocks.title: Remove -re, add -vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano
blocks.text: The imperfetto is the most regular tense in Italian: *parla-re → parlavo*, *vede-re → vedevo*, *dormi-re → dormivo*. Even most irregular verbs are regular here.

blocks.title: fare, dire, bere use their old stems
blocks.text: *fare → facevo*, *dire → dicevo*, *bere → bevevo* — from the older forms *facere, dicere, bevere*.

items: Habits and repeated actions in the past: *Da bambino giocavo sempre in giardino.* (As a child I always played in the garden.)
Descriptions of people, places, weather, time and age: *Era notte. Il bosco era buio. L'orso aveva sonno.*
States of mind and feelings: *Il topo aveva paura.*
Actions in progress at a moment in the past: *Alle otto dormivo.* (At eight I was sleeping.)
The fairy-tale opening: *C'era una volta…* (Once upon a time there was…).

blocks.title: English equivalents
blocks.text: The imperfetto corresponds to English 'used to + verb', 'was/were + -ing', or a simple past of description ('the wood was dark').

blocks.title: Polite or attenuated requests
blocks.text: With verbs such as *volere, venire, chiamare* the imperfetto softens a present request: *Volevo un caffè, per favore. Telefonavo per chiedere un’informazione.* The meaning is present; the past tense makes it less direct, like the condizionale (*vorrei*).

blocks.title: Intentions that did not happen
blocks.text: *Stavo per uscire* (I was about to go out), *Dovevo partire ieri* (I was supposed to leave yesterday — and perhaps did not).

blocks.title: Colloquial counterfactuals
blocks.text: In informal speech the imperfetto can replace both verbs of an unreal past hypothesis: *Se lo sapevo, venivo* for standard *Se l’avessi saputo, sarei venuto.* It is very common in conversation and is attested in literature, but it is not standard in formal writing. See the [[periodo-ipotetico|periodo ipotetico]].

blocks.title: Reported speech
blocks.text: After a past verb of saying, a present of direct speech becomes imperfetto: *«Ho fame»* → *Ha detto che aveva fame.* See [[discorso-indiretto|indirect speech]].

examples.it: C'era una volta un piccolo orso.
examples.en: Once upon a time there was a little bear.

examples.it: Era inverno e faceva freddo.
examples.en: It was winter and it was cold.

examples.it: Da bambina abitavo al mare.
examples.en: As a child I lived by the sea.

examples.it: Il nonno ci raccontava sempre delle storie.
examples.en: Grandfather always used to tell us stories.

examples.it: L'orso aveva sonno ma non dormiva.
examples.en: The bear was sleepy but wasn't sleeping.

examples.it: Alle otto i bambini dormivano.
examples.en: At eight the children were sleeping.

examples.it: Volevo un caffè, per favore.
examples.en: I’d like a coffee, please.
examples.note: Polite imperfetto: the request is in the present.

examples.it: Se lo sapevo, venivo.
examples.en: If I had known, I would have come.
examples.note: Colloquial; standard: Se l’avessi saputo, sarei venuto.

exercises.explanation: fare uses the stem face-: faceva.

mistakes.message: fare uses its old stem face-: faceva.

exercises.prompt: Complete the description with the imperfetto.
exercises.text: {0} (essere) notte. Il bosco {1} (essere) buio e {2} (fare) freddo. L'orso {3} (avere) sonno.
exercises.explanation: Descriptions of time, place, weather and states use the imperfetto.

exercises.prompt: Translate: As a child I lived by the sea. (male speaker)
accept: Quando ero bambino abitavo al mare.
Quando ero bambino vivevo al mare.
exercises.explanation: da bambino = as a child; a past situation → imperfetto.

exercises.prompt: Translate: *C'era una volta un piccolo orso.*
exercises.answer: Once upon a time there was a little bear.
accept: Once upon a time there was a small bear.
exercises.explanation: C'era una volta = once upon a time there was.

summary: Used for habits, descriptions, states, actions in progress, and C'era una volta.

title: Imperfetto or passato prossimo?
description: Background versus events: choosing the past tense in a story.
objectives: Use mentre with the imperfetto and quando with an interrupting event.
Narrate a short sequence in the past.

blocks.caption: Which tense?
rows: Events that move the story forward: *Il telefono ha squillato.*
A single occasion: *Quell'estate siamo andati in montagna.*
States without a clear end: *Avevo paura.*
A completed, bounded action: *Ho avuto paura per un momento.*

blocks.title: A useful test
blocks.text: Ask: is this the stage (imperfetto) or something that happens on the stage (passato prossimo)? A completed action with a clear beginning and end takes the passato prossimo; an ongoing situation or repeated habit takes the imperfetto.

blocks.title: Interrupted action
blocks.text: An action in progress (imperfetto) is interrupted by an event (passato prossimo): *Mentre dormivo, è arrivato il nonno.* / *Dormivo quando è arrivato il nonno.*

blocks.title: Simultaneous background actions
blocks.text: Two things going on at the same time both take the imperfetto: *Mentre la mamma cucinava, io leggevo.*

examples.it: Era notte e pioveva.
examples.en: It was night and it was raining.

examples.it: Mentre dormivo, è arrivato il nonno.
examples.en: While I was sleeping, Grandfather arrived.

examples.it: Ogni estate andavamo al mare.
examples.en: Every summer we used to go to the seaside.

examples.it: Quell'estate siamo andati in montagna.
examples.en: That summer we went to the mountains.

examples.it: Il topo mangiava il formaggio quando è entrato il gatto.
examples.en: The mouse was eating the cheese when the cat came in.

examples.it: Mentre la mamma cucinava, io leggevo.
examples.en: While Mum was cooking, I was reading.

exercises.prompt: Mentre ___ (dormire, io), è arrivato il nonno.
Il topo mangiava il formaggio quando il gatto ___ (entrare).
exercises.explanation: The interrupting event → passato prossimo, with essere (entrare).

mistakes.message: Right tense, wrong auxiliary: entrare takes essere — è entrato.

exercises.text: {0} (essere) notte e {1} (piovere). All'improvviso l'orso {2} (sentire) un rumore.
exercises.explanation: Scene-setting → imperfetto; a sudden event → passato prossimo.

exercises.prompt: Translate: While Mum was cooking, I was reading.
exercises.answer: Mentre la mamma cucinava, io leggevo.
accept: Io leggevo mentre la mamma cucinava.
exercises.explanation: Two simultaneous background actions → both imperfetto.

summary: Imperfetto = the stage: background, description, habits, actions in progress.
Passato prossimo = events on the stage: completed actions.
mentre + imperfetto; an interrupting event in the passato prossimo.

title: Trapassato prossimo
description: The pluperfect: an action completed before another past moment. Formation, uses in narration and reported speech, and when the passato prossimo is used instead.
objectives: Form the trapassato prossimo with the imperfetto of avere or essere + past participle.
Use it for an action that precedes another past action or moment.
Use it in reported speech after a past reporting verb.
Distinguish it from the trapassato remoto, which is literary.

blocks.title: Imperfetto of the auxiliary + participle
blocks.text: *avevo mangiato* (I had eaten), *ero partito/a* (I had left). The auxiliary and the agreement follow exactly the same rules as in the passato prossimo.

blocks.title: Before another past moment
blocks.text: The trapassato prossimo places an action before a reference point that is already in the past: *Quando sono arrivato alla stazione, il treno era già partito.* The order of events is: the train left → I arrived.

blocks.title: Background in narration
blocks.text: In a story told in the passato prossimo or the passato remoto, it fills in what had happened earlier: *Sara era stanca: aveva lavorato tutto il giorno.*

blocks.title: Reported speech
blocks.text: After a past verb of saying or thinking, a passato prossimo of the direct speech becomes a trapassato prossimo: *«Ho finito»* → *Ha detto che aveva finito.* See the lesson on indirect speech.

blocks.title: When the order is obvious
blocks.text: If the sequence is already clear from the context or from words like *prima* or *dopo*, the passato prossimo is often used instead, especially in conversation: *Prima ho mangiato, poi sono uscito.* The trapassato is needed when the earlier event is mentioned after the later one.

blocks.title: Trapassato remoto
blocks.text: In literary narration in the passato remoto, an action that immediately precedes another, after *dopo che, appena, quando, (non) appena*, can be expressed with the trapassato remoto: *Dopo che ebbe mangiato, uscì.* It is limited to this construction and to writing; the trapassato prossimo is also correct there.

examples.it: Quando siamo arrivati, il film era già cominciato.
examples.en: When we arrived, the film had already started.

examples.it: Non avevo mai visto il mare prima di quel giorno.
examples.en: I had never seen the sea before that day.

examples.it: Sara era stanca perché aveva lavorato tutto il giorno.
examples.en: Sara was tired because she had worked all day.

examples.it: Marco ha detto che aveva perso le chiavi.
examples.en: Marco said that he had lost his keys.

examples.it: Avevo appena finito di mangiare quando è arrivata la nonna.
examples.en: I had just finished eating when Grandma arrived.

examples.it: Dopo che ebbe finito la lettera, la chiuse.
examples.en: After she had finished the letter, she closed it.

exercises.explanation: uscire takes essere: imperfetto of essere + uscito/usciti.

exercises.text: Quando sono arrivato, i miei amici {0} (mangiare) già e Sara {1} (andare) a casa.
exercises.explanation: Both events precede my arrival. andare takes essere; andata agrees with Sara.

exercises.prompt: *Quando ho chiamato, Luca era già uscito.* What happened first?
options: they happened at the same time
exercises.explanation: The trapassato (era uscito) marks the earlier event.

exercises.prompt: Report it: *«Ho finito i compiti»*, ha detto Anna. → Anna ha detto che ___ i compiti.
exercises.explanation: Past reporting verb: passato prossimo → trapassato prossimo.

mistakes.message: This is possible in casual speech, but the standard sequence after ha detto is the trapassato: aveva finito.

exercises.prompt: Translate: I had never seen a wolf.
exercises.answer: Non avevo mai visto un lupo.
accept: Io non avevo mai visto un lupo.
Non avevo mai veduto un lupo.
exercises.explanation: mai goes between the auxiliary and the participle, as in the passato prossimo.

exercises.prompt: *Dopo che ___ la lettera, la chiuse.* Which option is the traditional literary choice?
exercises.explanation: With a passato remoto main clause, dopo che + trapassato remoto is the literary choice; aveva scritto is also correct.

summary: Trapassato prossimo = imperfetto of avere/essere + participle (avevo fatto, ero partito/a).
It marks an action completed before another past moment.
In reported speech, passato prossimo → trapassato prossimo after a past reporting verb.
With prima/poi or clear order, conversation often uses the passato prossimo; the trapassato remoto is literary.
